title: Canadian church arsons will be investigated by veteran fire marshal
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — A Canadian democracy group has hired a veteran fire investigator to look into the recent massive wave of arson attacks on Canadian churches over the past six years, with the goal being to provide his expert analysis on the incidents. In a statement posted October 15, The Democracy Fund (TDF) said they have chosen Glenn Baxter to lead the investigation into church and synagogue arsons. Baxter is currently serving as a fire marshal for a large Canadian fire department. According to the TDF, he has served in many communities in various roles from firefighter to fire chief. … As it stands now, arsons against religious institutions have skyrocketed in the last few years. Federal data show that there were 592 reported arsons from 2010 to 2022. However,some 423 of these acts of violence were from 2015 onward. In 2021 alone, there were 91 cases of arson, the same year the mainstream media ran with inflammatory and dubious claims that hundreds of children were buried and disregarded by Catholic priests and nuns who ran some Canadian residential schools. The reality is that, after four years, there have been no mass graves discovered at residential schools. However, amid the spread of the baseless claims, more than 100 churches, most of them Catholic and many of them on indigenous lands that serve the local population, have been burned to the ground, vandalized , or desecrated in Canada since the spring of 2021.

title: Trump signs bill to let priests opt back in to Social Security, Medicare
description: WASHINGTON, D.C. ( LifeSiteNews ) – President Donald Trump has signed bipartisan legislation giving religious clergy who previously opted out of Social Security or Medicare a new window to opt back in to receive benefits, giving them the option to secure peace of mind about their retirements. Federal law permits some religious figures to seek exemption from Social Security and Medicare taxes on their ministerial income, in exchange for not getting benefits from either program (unless another job gave them taxable income). Once made, that exemption is not reversible, though Congress has offered temporary windows for clergy to opt back in over the years. … “America’s pastors and faith leaders spend their lives caring for others. Many chose to opt out of Social Security when they were young and just starting their ministry,” said U.S. Rep. Jason Smith (R-MO), chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee. “A single, sometimes ill-advised, decision made decades ago should not stand between them and a secure retirement. The Clergy Act gives them a second chance.” “Our faith leaders dedicate their lives to serving others and strengthening our communities. The Clergy Act gives clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security the opportunity to re-enroll and secure their financial future,” added Rep. Vince Fong (R-CA). “I’m proud this bipartisan legislation passed both chambers of Congress and was signed into law by President Trump. Thank you to Senator Britt for her partnership and to President Trump for his leadership and commitment to our faith Meanwhile, the long-term solvency of Social Security for religious and secular beneficiaries alike is an ongoing concern, but agreement on how to reform the program remains elusive.
